Mahadev Kamble Since Deceased Through ... vs The State Of
Maharashtra on 6 December, 2024

Author: Surya Kant
Bench: Surya Kant
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Civil Appeal No.13993 Of 2024
 (Arising out of Slp(C) No.11897/2023)
 Mahadev Kamble Since Deceased
 Through Legal Heir Appellan
 Versus
 The State Of Maharashtra & Ors.
Responde
O R D E R
1. As per the office report, service is complete, but no one is present on behalf of the respondents.
2. Leave granted.
3. The appellants are aggrieved by the order dated 10.11.2022 passed by the High

Court of Judicature at Bombay, whereby their claim for making a reference under Section 28-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short, the 1894 Act), so as to enable them to seek same amount of compensation, as was granted to other expropriated land owners, has been dismissed on the ground that the order of the Lok Adalat relied upon by the appellants would not constitute an award on the basis of which the remedy under Section 28-A of the 1894 Act can be invoked.
4. We have heard learned counsel for the appellants.

5. It seems to us that if a reference made at the Section 18 of the 1894 Act, which is disposed of by the Reference Court pursuant to a settlement that has taken place in Lok Adalat, such consent order shall have all the ingredients of an award that may be passed by a Reference Court on merits under Section 18 of the 1894 Act.

In other words, if some of the land owners, affected by the same land acquisition process, have been awarded higher rate of compensation, be that as it may, on the basis of a settlement award passed by the Lok Adalat, such an order or award shall also meet with all the requirements of the 1894 Act for the purpose of accruing a cause of action for the left out land owners to invoke the jurisdiction of the Court under Section 28-A of the 1894 Act.

Any other construction will militate against the legislative object of Section 28-A of the 1894 Act, which is Mahadev Kamble Since Deceased Through ... vs The State Of Maharashtra on 6 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90197104/
1 founded upon the principle of equality in the matter of award of compensation.
6.

sentences.text: That being so, we are unable to approve of the reasons assigned by the High Court in declining to make reference under Section 28-A of the 1894 Act.
7. Consequently, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned order of the High Court is set aside.
Accordingly, the Reference Court is directed to decide the application, said to have been made by the appellants under Section 28-A of the 1894 Act.

8. We may hasten to add that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of maintainability of an application made under Section 28-A of 1894 Act in such circumstances,
which, according to the High Court, did not permit entertainment of such an application.
To say this differently, we have not expressed any opinion on the actual entitlement of the appellants for the same amount of compensation.
That is a question of fact, for which the parties will be permitted to lead their evidence and the Reference Court will determine the same on consideration thereof in accordance with law.
